note: Put the homepage's tile overlay on the four concern photographs on /pages/skin-concerns, so Malcolm can judge whether it reads better than the bare photo (2026-08-25). REVERSIBLE — remove_sections: ['concern_overlay_css'] takes it straight back off.
why_css_and_not_a_setting: The homepage tiles are 'image-link-blocks', where the link text sits ON the picture; its overlay is a real block setting (overlay_color #1a1a1a, overlay_opacity 40) rendered as --content-over-media-overlay. The concern sections here are 'multiple-images-with-text', where the text sits BESIDE the picture — that section's schema has no overlay setting at all. So the same effect has to be drawn in CSS. Theme Liquid is never edited (shopify.md rule 2); the additive custom-html section is the established pattern on this very template, which already carries one (banner_crop_anchor).
how_it_is_pinned_to_the_image: The image list is display:grid with width:100%, so a plain inset-0 ::after would bleed past the photo at the 1000-1150px breakpoint where the column is 0.8fr but the image caps at 500px. The ::after is instead placed in the photograph's own grid cell and given the same box rules the theme gives the img, so it tracks the picture exactly at every width.
two_faults_in_the_first_attempt_measured: WRONG CELL. theme.css puts the picture in column 2, not column 1: `.multiple-images-with-text__image-list:not([layout=stacked])>img:first-child{grid-area:1 / 2 / -1}`. My first pass tried to drag the img back to 1/1, but that theme selector scores (0,3,1) against my (0,2,1) and won, so the img stayed in column 2 while the overlay sat alone in an empty column 1. The fix is to move the OVERLAY to the img's cell, not the img to the overlay's.

WRONG PAINT ORDER. theme.css also sets `will-change:transform` on that img, which makes it a stacking context painted in the positioned layer at z-index 0 — above any non-positioned ::after, however it is placed. The overlay therefore rendered *behind* the photograph. The ::after needs position:relative + z-index:1 to sit on top.

Either fault alone produces a page that looks completely untouched, which is exactly what the first push did: a full-page capture before and after was identical to the pixel outside the announcement bar. The CSS was on the page and verbatim correct-looking the whole time — reading the served HTML would have 'confirmed' it worked.

settings.html:
<style>
  /* The homepage tile overlay, drawn on a section whose schema has no overlay setting. */
  .shopify-section--multiple-images-with-text .multiple-images-with-text__image-list::after {
    content: "";
    /* the photograph's own cell - theme.css puts it in column 2, not column 1 */
    grid-area: 1 / 2 / -1;
    /* the theme gives that img will-change:transform, so only a positioned
       box with a z-index paints above it */
    position: relative;
    z-index: 1;
    /* mirror the img's box so the wash tracks the picture, not the column */
    width: 100%;
    max-width: var(--multiple-images-with-text-image-max-width, 390px);
    margin-inline: auto;
    align-self: stretch;
    background: rgb(26 26 26 / 0.4);
    border-radius: var(--rounded-sm);
    pointer-events: none;
  }
</style>
